name: The Lebanon Oak of the Tiergarten

location.address: Grosser Tiergarten, east of the Englischer Garten, Berlin-Mitte

access: Free, open public park (Grosser Tiergarten), no gate; open at all hours.
transport: S Bellevue (S3/S5/S7/S9), roughly 400 m, 5 to 8 minutes on foot.
verify_notes: Register reason is rarity: Quercus libani is a Near Eastern oak uncommon in Berlin. A WebSearch summary claimed a circumference of 1825 for this tree; that figure is a land-parcel (Flurstueck) number repeated across five unrelated Tiergarten rows in the 2021 ordinance, NOT a girth. name: The Zehlendorf Peace Oak

location.address: In front of Clayallee 357, corner Potsdamer Strasse / Berliner Strasse, Berlin-Zehlendorf

access: Free, on the public road junction at the centre of Zehlendorf; there was a bench round the trunk until the root zone was unsealed after 2020 (de.wikipedia).
transport: S Zehlendorf (S1), roughly 340 m, about 5 minutes on foot (OSM platform to register point).
verify_notes: Planted 2 September 1871, the first anniversary of the Battle of Sedan, as a Friedenseiche (peace oak) after the Franco-Prussian War; a bronze plaque on the south side of the trunk says so (de.wikipedia 'Zehlendorfer Eiche', fetched as wikitext). Documented planting date for THIS tree, so age 1871 is a source figure (about 155 years in 2026). Naturdenkmal 6-31/B (X-42B), designated 1993-03-02 for regional-heritage reasons ('Schoenheit, landeskundliche Gruende' in the register). A large limb broke in June 2020 in rush-hour traffic (Berliner Morgenpost 2020-06-16); the area round the oak was to be unsealed to give the roots room and the bench was removed. Alive: lifecheck RECENT 2025-06-04 (Commons photo at the spot) plus the Wikipedia article's 2020 account; a 2025 photo is the nearest to a recent confirmation, so say how the crown looks after the 2020 loss only from a photo. Dominates the junction with Heimatmuseum Zehlendorf and the Dorfkirche beside it. PIN: register coordinate 52.435324,13.260262 and Wikipedia/Wikidata 52.435332,13.260241 (about 2 m apart; same ordinance origin) at a single dominant crown on an open junction, so confirmed; Commons photo is not geotagged. PHOTO CANDIDATE (not approved, unlooked): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Zehlendorf_Friedenseiche.JPG , CC BY-SA 3.0, by Kvikk, 2013-06-06, 2928x2168 (11 years old; summer, in leaf; would need a fresher frame if the crown changed after 2020). Girth not published in any source seen.

name: The 500-Year Oak of Berlin Zoo

location.address: Zoologischer Garten Berlin, south of the hippo house, Hardenbergplatz 8, Berlin-Charlottenburg

access: Paid entry: inside the Zoologischer Garten Berlin, ticket required (check current Zoo prices and hours before visiting).
transport: S/U Zoologischer Garten, the Hardenbergplatz entrance is about 200 m from the register point; inside the zoo, a few minutes' walk.
verify_notes: REGISTER: Naturdenkmal 1-52/B, Stiel-Eiche, 'Zoologischer Garten, suedlich Flusspferdhaus, Hardenbergplatz 8', designated 1993-03-02, reasons Eigenart and landeskundliche Gruende; tree-level register coordinate 52.508685,13.336639. AGE: the zoo's own park article (Stadt und Gruen, fetched directly) has a numbered feature 'Schatten seit 500 Jahren: Die ewige Eiche (Columbus-Eiche / Pedunculate Oak)' and says the historic oak stock is to be preserved, and says the zoo holds eleven Naturdenkmaeler. A Commons photo uploaded by User:Istriana is captioned 'ungefaehr 500 Jahre alte Eiche, Naturdenkmal' for the same Wikidata item. LIMIT: no fetched source states in so many words that the 'ewige Eiche' IS register tree 1-52/B (it is the only ND oak the register lists in the zoo, and the Commons caption ties the 500-year figure to the Naturdenkmal, but this is two inferences, not one statement), and 500 years is a round figure from the owner with no method. Deliver flagged; the writer says 'about 500 years, according to the zoo'. A Quercus robur of 500 years in central Berlin is plausible as a remnant of the pre-park Tiergarten oaks but that is NOT sourced; do not write it. PIN: approximate because the Commons photo is not geotagged, so only the register point supports it; it is a tree-level point inside the zoo (a plan or aerial view would settle it). ALIVE: lifecheck RECENT 2024-10-09 (iNaturalist observation 246793865 at the point) plus the 2024-06-25 Commons photo.
